reason: Transcription typo in Challoner's note, not in his text: 'comdemnation' for 'condemnation' (m for n). A mechanical single-letter defect of the kind pipeline/docs/corrections.md's policy admits -- no wording is changed, and the corrected reading is the only English word the letters can be.
evidence: corpus/raw/vulgata-online/DR2/Jo.3.json, record tp='fn' vn=19 rn=1: '_The judgment:_ That is, the cause of his comdemnation.' The note glosses John 3:19 'And this is the judgment', and the printed Challoner reads 'condemnation' -- cf. the note on the neighbouring verse 18 in the same chapter, which uses the word correctly twice ('is not condemned', 'condemned already'). 'comdemnation' is not a word, an archaism, or an eighteenth-century spelling.

reason: Transcription typo in the note's lemma: the two middle vowels are transposed. Mechanical and single-word, so within pipeline/docs/corrections.md's policy. It matters more than an ordinary typo because a lemma is structural, not prose -- it names the words in the verse the note glosses, and a lemma matching no string in its verse cannot be resolved to a span by anything downstream.
evidence: Internal: across the whole DR2 source the city is spelled 'Ninive' 13 times -- in verses (Gen 10:11-12, Tob 1:11, Jdt 1:5, Jonas 1:2 itself), in Jonas's own chapter argument, in Tobias's book preface, and in four OTHER footnotes including Nahum's -- against this single 'Nineve'. External: drbo.org, an independent transcription of the same Challoner apparatus, prints the note as '[2] "Ninive": The capital city of the Assyrian empire.' -- same gloss word for word, lemma spelled Ninive (https://drbo.org/chapter/37001.htm, retrieved 2026-08-24). Note that the missing inline anchor on this verse is a SEPARATE defect of the same transcription and is not repaired here: drbo marks the lemma in the verse text, vulgata.online does not.
